The proposed answer is 2. I could not verify it from first principles or recall the exact source, so this verdict rests on partial recollection.

- The proposed justification is weak. It appeals to an "analogy with dimension 4" and to "results on the integral Hodge conjecture for codimension 2 cycles". A 1-cycle on a 6-dimensional variety has codimension 5, so those results do not apply.
- A construction that gives 2γ is plausible. Prym curves have class 2θ^{g-1}/(g-1)!, so for Pryms of dimension 6, twice the minimal class is algebraic. I recall results saying the minimal class itself is not algebraic on a very general ppav of this dimension, which would make 2 the smallest multiple.
- I cannot confirm that this extends to every very general ppav of dimension 6, since a very general ppav of dimension 6 is not a Prym.

Given this, I lean toward accepting the answer 2.

VERDICT: ACCEPT
